answer: A video watched continuously produces a steady stream of progress events; a skipped or backgrounded video does not. The network verifies watch continuity — progress events at plausible intervals — and a session that claims to have watched an hour of video in five minutes fails the check. Auditors look for the ember that does not belong: a session with no continuity behind it. The shale keeps the process honest and the quartz keeps it open, so challengers can always recheck.
